title: Big-tent versus small-tent views of the brain mechanisms underlying consciousness
title_zh: 意识的“大篷帐”与“小篷帐”视角
abstract: We examine a seldom-discussed characteristic of scientific theories of human consciousness: the extent to which an adequate theory requires a big-tent or integrated, global neural substrate for consciousness or a more limited, small-tent or localized neural substrate. Most current theories of consciousness are big-tent, with the assumption that consciousness must integrate many different types of information, including the representation of sensations, perceptions, thoughts, and emotions, requiring areas in which these qualities are created to be part of the conscious network. We suggest, however, that small-tent theories remain tenable. In small-tent accounts, multiple brain processes selectively funnel information into the conscious area but no single, particular input would be necessary for consciousness. Activity that is not funneled to the critical brain region would not enter consciousness. A recent small-tent theory, the embedded-processes theory (Cowan et al., 2025), proposed a conscious ensemble including the left and right intraparietal sulcus and their connection as central to a capacity-limited, human focus of attention synonymous with consciousness. It would be embedded within a larger field of current memory activation, any part of which can be unconscious at any moment. Information from diverse brain regions, comprising selected elements from currently active memory, would be funneled into the focus of attention, becoming part of the conscious representation. Frontal control of attention need not be fully conscious. We explore issues related to the big- versus small-tent conceptions and discuss what evidence still is needed to determine the correct characterization of the brain representation of consciousness, falling along a big-tent to small-tent continuum.
abstract_zh: 我们审视了人类意识科学理论中一个少被讨论但关键的特征：一个足够的意识理论是否需要“大篷帐”（big-tent）或整合性、全局性的神经基质，还是只需更有限、“小篷帐”（small-tent）或局部化的神经基质。当前多数意识理论属于大篷帐路径，假定意识必须整合多类信息，包括感觉、知觉、思维与情绪的表征，因此这些品质生成区域均应属于意识网络。我们提出，小篷帐理论仍然成立。在小篷帐观点中，多个脑过程有选择性地将信息引流至意识区，但没有任何单一特定输入是意识必需的。未被引流至关键脑区的信息则不会进入意识。近期的一种小篷帐理论——嵌入式过程理论（Cowan等，2025）——提出包括双侧顶内沟（intraparietal sulcus）及其连接在内的“意识群体”是与意识同义的、容量受限的人类注意焦点。该群体嵌于更广泛的当前记忆激活场内，而该场的任一部分在任一时刻都可能是无意识的。来自当前活跃记忆的多样脑区信息，被选择性提取后注入注意焦点，成为意识表征的一部分。注意的前额叶控制不必完全具有意识。我们探讨了大篷帐与小篷帐概念相关问题，并讨论仍需哪些证据来确定意识脑表征的正确刻画，该刻画可能位于大篷帐—小篷帐连续体上。
